metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen subsequent forecast peaks.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast to show stronger upward momentum.
- Model tends to overestimate mean reversion in short-term (1-3 day) horizons; apply slight downward bias for 1-3 day forecasts.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility and ignores sentiment-driven mean reversion — apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce forecast divergence.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often forecasts a rebound too early — delay upward forecast triggers until sentiment stabilizes.
